conditions.cause: Fungus spread by wind and infected seed; worse after heavy nitrogen fertilizer.
conditions.chemical: Tricyclazole or azoxystrobin-class fungicide, following the product label. Spray early, before neck infection.
conditions.favorable: Cool nights, long leaf wetness, heavy dew
conditions.name: Rice blast
conditions.organic: Remove infected leaves, reduce nitrogen, plant resistant varieties, spray fermented garlic or neem extract as a protectant.
conditions.prevention: Use certified seed, avoid excess urea, keep spacing wide for airflow, rotate with legumes.

symptoms.text: Diamond-shaped grey spots with brown edges on leaves
Dark rotten neck below the panicle; grain turns empty
White empty panicles standing upright
Leaf tips dry and burn as spots join together

conditions.cause: Bacteria entering through wounds and water; spread by wind-driven rain and irrigation water.
conditions.chemical: Copper-based bactericide or streptomycin-class product where registered, following the label. Antibiotics are a last resort.
conditions.favorable: Windy rain, flooded fields, warm humid weather
conditions.name: Bacterial leaf blight
conditions.organic: Drain the field briefly, remove infected plants, spray copper-free plant extracts such as betel leaf; keep tools clean.
conditions.prevention: Resistant varieties, certified seed, balanced fertilizer, avoid flooding with contaminated water.

symptoms.text: Water-soaked stripes along leaf edges
Yellow-white stripes that dry and wilt the leaf
Young plants wilt and die completely (kresek)
Yellow bacterial ooze on cut leaves in the morning

conditions.cause: Sap-sucking insect; outbreaks follow heavy insecticide use that kills its natural enemies, plus excess nitrogen.
conditions.chemical: Pymetrozine or dinotefuran-class insecticide where registered, following the label. Never spray broad-spectrum insecticide early in the season.
conditions.favorable: Dense canopy, excess nitrogen, warm humid weather
conditions.name: Brown planthopper
conditions.organic: Drain the field for 2-3 days, conserve spiders and mirid bugs, use light traps at night, spray neem seed extract.
conditions.prevention: Resistant varieties, wide spacing, avoid early insecticide sprays, synchronous planting with neighbours.

symptoms.text: Round patches of dry brown plants (hopperburn)
Small brown insects clustered at the plant base
Sticky honeydew and black sooty mold on leaves
Plants stunted and yellowing from the base upward

conditions.cause: Moth larvae boring into the stem; moths lay eggs on leaves near water. Covers the yellow stem borer complex (several Scirpophaga species, incl. S. incertulas and S. innotata).
conditions.chemical: Cartap or chlorantraniliprole-class insecticide where registered, following the label, timed to egg hatching.
conditions.favorable: Staggered planting, stubbles left in the field, warm nights
conditions.name: Rice stem borer
conditions.organic: Cut stubbles low after harvest, use pheromone or light traps, release Trichogramma parasitoids, hand-pick egg masses.
conditions.prevention: Synchronous planting, destroy stubbles, avoid late planting, use resistant varieties.

symptoms.text: Dead central shoot that pulls out easily (deadheart)
White empty panicles (whitehead) at heading
Small entry holes on the stem with frass
White-yellow moths flying over the field at dusk

conditions.cause: Fungus spread by rain splash and infected seed; worst in wet weather on ripe fruit.
conditions.chemical: Mancozeb or azoxystrobin-class fungicide, following the label, starting at flowering.
conditions.favorable: Rainy weather, ripe fruit, poor drainage
conditions.name: Chili anthracnose
conditions.organic: Pick and bury infected fruit, mulch to stop soil splash, spray fermented garlic or turmeric extract, improve drainage.
conditions.prevention: Certified seed, wide spacing, drip irrigation, harvest ripe fruit promptly, rotate crops.

symptoms.text: Sunken black circular spots on ripe fruit
Orange-pink spore rings inside the spots
Fruit rots and drops before harvest
Small dark spots on leaves and stems

conditions.cause: Soil bacteria blocking the water vessels; spread by water, tools, and infected seedlings.
conditions.chemical: No effective curative treatment exists for Ralstonia. Copper bactericide may protect adjacent healthy plants as a barrier spray; always follow the label.
conditions.favorable: Warm wet soil, acidic soil, waterlogged beds
conditions.name: Bacterial wilt
conditions.organic: Uproot and burn infected plants, solarise the soil, lime acidic soil, plant resistant varieties or grafted seedlings.
conditions.prevention: Resistant varieties, raised beds, clean water, crop rotation with non-hosts, disinfect tools.

symptoms.text: Sudden wilting of green leaves on hot days
Wilting without yellowing; leaves stay green
Milky bacterial ooze from a cut stem in water
Whole plant collapses within days

conditions.cause: Tiny sap-sucking insects; also vectors of viruses. Worst in hot dry weather.
conditions.chemical: Spinetoram or abamectin-class insecticide where registered, following the label. Rotate modes of action.
conditions.favorable: Hot dry weather, young tender shoots
conditions.name: Thrips
conditions.organic: Blue and yellow sticky traps, spray neem oil, conserve predatory mites, mulch with silver plastic.
conditions.prevention: Clean seedlings, reflective mulch, avoid planting next to infested fields, weed control.

symptoms.text: Young leaves curl upward and turn silvery
Silvery streaks and scarring on leaves and fruit
Stunted shoots with deformed flowers
Tiny slender yellow-black insects under young leaves

conditions.cause: Sap-sucking insects that also spread viruses; thrive on soft new growth after heavy nitrogen.
conditions.chemical: Imidacloprid or pymetrozine-class insecticide where registered, following the label. Avoid spraying during flowering.
conditions.favorable: Soft new growth, excess nitrogen, warm weather
conditions.name: Aphids
conditions.organic: Strong water spray to knock them off, neem oil or soap spray, conserve ladybirds and lacewings, plant marigold borders.
conditions.prevention: Balanced fertilizer, reflective mulch, remove weeds that host aphids, inspect seedlings before transplanting.

symptoms.text: Clusters of small green insects under leaves
Sticky honeydew with black sooty mold
Leaves curl and yellow where aphids feed
Ants farming the aphids on the plant

conditions.cause: Fungus surviving in soil and debris; splashed upward by rain onto lower leaves.
conditions.chemical: Chlorothalonil or mancozeb-class fungicide, following the label, from early growth onward.
conditions.favorable: Warm wet leaves, rain splash, stressed plants
conditions.name: Early blight
conditions.organic: Remove lower leaves, mulch thickly, spray fermented garlic or baking-soda solution, space plants for airflow.
conditions.prevention: Rotate with non-solanaceous crops, stake plants, water at the base, clean up debris after harvest.

symptoms.text: Brown spots with concentric rings (bullseye) on lower leaves
Yellowing around the spots as leaves die upward
Dark cankers on stems near the soil
Dark leathery rot at the stem end of fruit

conditions.cause: Water mold spread by wind and rain; can destroy a field in days in cool wet weather.
conditions.chemical: Metalaxyl or mandipropamid-class fungicide, following the label. Act at the first spot — it spreads fast.
conditions.favorable: Cool wet nights, long leaf wetness, dense canopy
conditions.name: Late blight
conditions.organic: Remove infected plants immediately, improve airflow, copper-free plant extracts only slow it; resistant varieties are the best defence.
conditions.prevention: Resistant varieties, wide spacing, avoid overhead watering, destroy volunteer potatoes and tomatoes.

symptoms.text: Dark water-soaked spots on leaves that turn brown fast
White fuzzy mold under leaves in humid mornings
Dark rotting stems and whole plant collapse
Firm brown rot spreading across green fruit

conditions.cause: Soil fungus entering roots and blocking water vessels; survives years in soil.
conditions.chemical: No cure once infected. Soil fumigation is costly and restricted in many places — check local rules.
conditions.favorable: Warm soil, acidic soil, short rotations
conditions.name: Fusarium wilt
conditions.organic: Uproot and burn infected plants, solarise soil, add compost and Trichoderma, lime acidic soil, use resistant varieties.
conditions.prevention: Resistant varieties or grafted seedlings, long rotation, clean seedlings, raised beds with fresh soil.

symptoms.text: Yellowing and wilting on one side of the plant first
Brown streaks inside a cut stem
Wilting moves upward as lower leaves die
Plants do not recover overnight or after watering

conditions.cause: Moth caterpillars boring into fruit; eggs hatch on leaves and larvae move to fruit.
conditions.chemical: Chlorantraniliprole or emamectin-class insecticide where registered, following the label, timed to young larvae.
conditions.favorable: Warm nights, flowering and fruiting stage
conditions.name: Tomato fruitworm
conditions.organic: Hand-pick caterpillars, spray Bt (Bacillus thuringiensis) or neem, use pheromone traps, plant marigold as a trap crop.
conditions.prevention: Pheromone traps, destroy crop residue, rotate crops, inspect fruit twice a week.

symptoms.text: Round holes bored into fruit with frass
Green-brown caterpillars inside fruit or on leaves
Eaten flower buds and young fruit
Brown moths active at dusk laying eggs on leaves

conditions.cause: Oomycete fungus spread by wind-borne spores in wet weather and by infected seed.
conditions.chemical: Metalaxyl-class seed treatment or foliar fungicide where registered, following the label. Early action is essential.
conditions.favorable: Wet mornings, young plants, susceptible varieties
conditions.name: Downy mildew
conditions.organic: Rogue out infected plants early, use resistant varieties, treat seed with hot water or botanical extracts, improve drainage.
conditions.prevention: Resistant varieties, certified seed, early planting, remove infected plants before spores spread.

symptoms.text: Pale yellow-white streaks along leaves
Grey-white downy growth under leaves in the morning
Severely stunted plants with narrow pale leaves
Infected plants form no cob or a tiny deformed cob

conditions.cause: Invasive moth caterpillar; moths fly long distances and lay eggs in batches on leaves.
conditions.chemical: Spinetoram or emamectin-class insecticide where registered, following the label, aimed into the whorl at young larvae.
conditions.favorable: Young maize, warm weather, late planting
conditions.name: Fall armyworm
conditions.organic: Crush egg masses, drop sand or ash mixed with neem into whorls, spray Bt or neem, conserve earwigs and parasitoids.
conditions.prevention: Early planting, intercrop with legumes, pheromone traps, scout twice weekly from emergence.

symptoms.text: Windowpane feeding holes on young leaves
Moist sawdust-like frass in the leaf whorl
Brown caterpillar with inverted-Y mark on its head
Ragged shredded whorl leaves on young plants

conditions.cause: Fungus surviving in debris; spores spread by wind in humid weather.
conditions.chemical: Azoxystrobin or propiconazole-class fungicide where registered, following the label, at early symptoms.
conditions.favorable: Cool humid weather, dew, dense canopy
conditions.name: Northern corn leaf blight
conditions.organic: Bury debris by ploughing, rotate crops, use resistant varieties, improve airflow with proper spacing.
conditions.prevention: Resistant varieties, debris management, rotation with non-hosts, balanced fertilizer.

symptoms.text: Long grey-green cigar-shaped lesions on leaves
Lesions spread from lower to upper leaves
Leaves dry and die, leaving a scorched look
Poor grain filling on badly infected plants

conditions.cause: Moth larvae boring into stems; eggs laid on leaves of young plants. Asian corn borer (Ostrinia furnacalis); the stalk-borer complex can also include Sesamia species.
conditions.chemical: Cartap or chlorantraniliprole-class insecticide where registered, following the label, before larvae enter the stem.
conditions.favorable: Late planting, stubbles left in the field
conditions.name: Maize stalk borer
conditions.organic: Destroy stubbles after harvest, use light traps, release Trichogramma, hand-pick egg masses.
conditions.prevention: Early planting, destroy stubbles, rotate with legumes, avoid late sowing.

symptoms.text: Dead central shoot on young plants
Rows of small holes across unfolding leaves
Tunnels and frass inside the stem
Stems break and lodge in wind

conditions.cause: Fungus spread by wind and rain; worst when leaves stay wet and bulbs are wounded.
conditions.chemical: Mancozeb or chlorothalonil-class fungicide, following the label, from early leaf growth.
conditions.favorable: Wet leaves, rain, warm humid weather
conditions.name: Purple blotch
conditions.organic: Remove infected leaves, mulch, spray fermented garlic, dry bulbs well before storage, cure in the sun.
conditions.prevention: Healthy seed bulbs, wide spacing, avoid overhead watering, rotate with rice, cure bulbs properly.

symptoms.text: Purple spots with yellow halos on leaves
Leaf tips dry and die back from the spots
Bulbs rot from the neck in storage
Small poorly filled bulbs at harvest

conditions.cause: Soil fungus entering through the basal plate; survives years in soil and on seed bulbs.
conditions.chemical: No cure once infected. Carbendazim-class seed-bulb treatment where registered, following the label, is preventive only.
conditions.favorable: Warm soil, waterlogged beds, infected seed bulbs
conditions.name: Fusarium basal rot
conditions.organic: Dip seed bulbs in hot water or Trichoderma solution, solarise soil, add compost, lime acidic soil.
conditions.prevention: Healthy seed bulbs, long rotation, raised beds with good drainage, dry bulbs thoroughly before storage.

symptoms.text: Leaves yellow and wilt from the tips down
Soft brown rot at the bulb base with white-pink mold
Plants pull out easily because roots are rotten
Bulbs rot in storage starting from the base

conditions.cause: Tiny sap-sucking insects hiding in leaf folds; worst in hot dry weather.
conditions.chemical: Spinetoram or abamectin-class insecticide where registered, following the label. Spray into leaf folds.
conditions.favorable: Hot dry weather, young leaves
conditions.name: Onion thrips
conditions.organic: Blue sticky traps, neem oil spray, keep plants well watered, mulch, conserve predatory mites.
conditions.prevention: Clean seed bulbs, avoid planting next to infested onions, weed control, reflective mulch.

symptoms.text: Silvery-white streaks and speckles on leaves
Leaves twist and curl as they dry
Tiny pale insects hiding inside leaf folds
Small bulbs when attack is heavy early on

conditions.cause: Moth caterpillars feeding at night; moths lay eggs in batches on leaves.
conditions.chemical: Emamectin or chlorantraniliprole-class insecticide where registered, following the label, on young larvae.
conditions.favorable: Warm nights, dense weeds, young plants
conditions.name: Armyworm
conditions.organic: Hand-pick caterpillars at night, spray Bt or neem, use pheromone and light traps, plant trap crops.
conditions.prevention: Scout twice weekly, destroy egg masses, rotate crops, keep field edges clean of weeds.

symptoms.text: Leaves eaten from the edges, sometimes to the midrib
Small green caterpillars feeding at night
Dark frass pellets on leaves and soil
Damage appears overnight while plants looked fine in the evening

conditions.cause: Wind-borne rust fungus; spores travel long distances and infect fast in wet weather.
conditions.chemical: Triazole or strobilurin-class fungicide, following the label, at first symptoms — it spreads fast.
conditions.favorable: Long leaf wetness, warm humid weather, dense canopy
conditions.name: Soybean rust
conditions.organic: Remove infected leaves, use resistant varieties, improve airflow, spray fermented garlic as a protectant.
conditions.prevention: Resistant varieties, early planting, wide spacing, scout lower leaves weekly, destroy volunteer soybeans.

symptoms.text: Small brown spots on lower leaves
Tiny raised pustules with powdery spores under leaves
Rapid yellowing and leaf drop from the bottom up
Severe defoliation before pods fill

conditions.cause: Bacteria spread by rain splash and wind; enters through leaf pores and wounds.
conditions.chemical: Copper-based bactericide, following the label, as a protectant only. No cure for infected leaves.
conditions.favorable: Rainy weather, warm temperatures, wet leaves
conditions.name: Bacterial pustule
conditions.organic: Remove infected leaves, avoid working in wet fields, use resistant varieties, rotate crops.
conditions.prevention: Certified seed, resistant varieties, rotation with cereals, avoid overhead irrigation.

symptoms.text: Small yellow-green spots on leaves
Raised brown pustules in the centre of spots
Spots without the wide yellow halo of other blights
Leaves drop early when attack is heavy

conditions.cause: Moth caterpillars boring into pods and eating seeds; eggs laid on young pods.
conditions.chemical: Chlorantraniliprole or emamectin-class insecticide where registered, following the label, at early podding.
conditions.favorable: Flowering and podding stage, warm nights
conditions.name: Pod borer
conditions.organic: Hand-pick infested pods, spray Bt or neem at flowering, use pheromone traps, plant early.
conditions.prevention: Early planting, pheromone traps, destroy residue, rotate with cereals, scout pods weekly.

symptoms.text: Small holes in pods with webbing inside
Pinkish-green caterpillar eating seeds inside the pod
Pods empty or half-eaten at harvest
Small grey moths around the crop at dusk

conditions.cause: Sap-sucking insects that also transmit viruses; thrive in hot dry weather on young plants.
conditions.chemical: Pymetrozine or acetamiprid-class insecticide where registered, following the label. Rotate modes of action.
conditions.favorable: Hot dry weather, young plants, dense canopy
conditions.name: Whitefly
conditions.organic: Yellow sticky traps, neem oil spray, conserve parasitoid wasps, reflective mulch, remove virus-infected plants.
conditions.prevention: Reflective mulch, clean seedlings, remove virus hosts and weeds, avoid planting next to infested fields.

symptoms.text: Clouds of tiny white flies rising when plants are shaken
Sticky honeydew and black sooty mold on leaves
Leaves yellow and curl where whiteflies feed
Mosaic yellowing — whiteflies also spread viruses
